Synthetix integrations and observed research-wallet activity
1 October 2026. Blockchain work remains read-only. This inventory covers the official pre-fork ecosystem
catalogue, selected historical integration reports and proposals, the local DirectIntegrationManager
event history, and SNX/sUSD transfers involving five examined wallets. It distinguishes historical
integration, current local configuration, observed use and administrative control.
The strongest new finding is actual use of the local DAI/sUSD wrapper. Five successful transactions
from e121 deposited 136,554.715815649876218232 pDAI in total and issued 
136,213.329026110751527686 sUSD to that wallet after its 25-basis-point mint fee. This proves a
working local collateral-to-synth route at those historical executions. It does not prove fresh private-L2
issuance or control of Synthetix governance.
What was examined
The official Gitbook repository is pinned to commit 2de4381a605d7a7b9f03d08164a0f29b7ea629b7, dated 8 May
2023. All 19 selected integration/ecosystem Markdown files are saved. The SIP repository is pinned to 
3b6b70f137cd6b0a23c39daceaa76f80cdbc520a, dated 9 May 2023. A complete archive search found 31 proposals
with titles matching the recorded integration/bridge/wrapper/ecosystem terms; their pre-fork statuses
are retained. A second full-archive search associates all eleven locally discovered integration addresses
with their published SIP/SCCP records.
This is a complete inventory of those defined source sets and the selected manager's queried event
history. Permissionless token use has no universal registry: it would be misleading to call this proof of
every application ever interacting with SNX or a synth. Private-L2 installations and every intervening
wallet are outside the accessible scope.
Historical integrations relevant to the thesis
The functions below are documented historical connections. Their presence in a source report does not
certify a presently working PulseChain or private-L2 route.

Primary evidence for the catalogue and exchange integrations is the pinned official ecosystem, SIP-288, 
SIP-296, and the Q3 2022 report. The Q4 2022 report identifies Beefy, Granary, Sonne, Hop and Silo; the 
Q1 2023 report identifies Unidex and distinguishes Mux/Nested work still in progress.
The 2022 ecosystem guide records Thales, Aelin and Velodrome connections. The 2022 milestone review
records debt hedging and Gelato claims. Aave's 2020 integration announcement and the Curve/iearn
liquidity trial establish earlier links. The local mStable and pool connections are verified separately in the
issuer study (Appendix 38) and sUSD route study (Appendix 66).
Other links, proposals and data services
The historical volume program names SNX.Link, Pillar Wallet, ParaSwap, dHEDGE, Kwenta and Solidefi.
This is frontend/referral history, not certification of present liquidity or administrative privileges.
The Q2/Q4 reports also record governance participation or outreach involving Euler, Gearbox, Across,
Alchemix, SushiSwap, Dodo, MetaMask, Matcha, Zapper, Zerion, Bankless Academy and EthernautDAO.
Outreach is not an implemented token route. Mux and Nested are explicitly in progress in the selected
Q1 2023 source. Fixed Forex's special direct-integration proposal SIP-292 is rejected at the pinned
boundary, as are the proposed special Curve integration in SIP-268 and peg-balancing integration in
SIP-2007. Existing ordinary markets must not be confused with these unimplemented proposed
privileges.
Data/tooling connections in the pinned Gitbook include The Graph subgraphs, DefiLlama and CryptoFees/
CryptoStats adapters, and Kwenta's Python SDK. Tracking codes attribute trading activity and revenue;
they do not appoint their users as owners.

These are exchange volume settings, not wrapper collateral caps or permission to mint arbitrary
tokens. Four addresses retain differences from default; historical configuration does not establish a
continuing benefit for the other seven. The 1967 substring in 0x6092…3741 is not the research wallet ending
in 1967.
SIP-267 and the integrity-checked pre-fork npm source describe owner-controlled parameter overrides.
The current owner getter remains the Synthetix Safe. The manager and eleven integration explorer
responses lack verified source bodies, so address attribution rests on published proposals, saved events
and current getter results, not independent compilation. All eleven have nonempty sampled runtime.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 443

Five research wallets—1967, feca, BAD9, e121 and a301—receive the default exchange parameters for
all three tested keys. This does not prevent them from trading through an integration contract. Sampled
sUSD rate validity is clear, but sETH and sBTC are rate-invalid. Consequently historical atomic ETH/BTC
routes cannot be promoted into verified present operation.
Optimism has distinct direct integrations in implemented SIP-2006 for Lyra
(0xbfa31380ed380ceb325153ea08f296a45a489108) and SIP-2008 for Polynomial
(0x3349de7822aa05f857e92d167b264809419dc620). Those historical L2 addresses are not entries in this local L1
census; their current private-L2 state is unverified.

pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 444

Historical iearn ySUSD at 0xf61718057901f84c4eec4339ef8f0d86d2b45600 and bZx LoanT oken at 
0x49f4592e641820e928f9919ef4abd92a719b4b49, appearing in 1967 activity.
The ySUSD source names existing local sUSD as its underlying and contains lending-allocation
interfaces. This demonstrates a local receipt/custody option; it does not certify current yield or every
configured downstream lender. The LoanT oken transaction calls mint(address,uint256) but transfers 999
existing sUSD from 1967 into the lending contract. It mints a lending receipt, not fresh sUSD.
Symbolic function names alone would give the wrong interpretation.
T wenty-four distinct transaction targets are retained in activity-selected-source-and-trace-index.json,
including unresolved source responses. Unverified targets are not assigned speculative protocol names.
A token transfer involving a router or vault demonstrates that transaction's asset movement; it is not
proof that the wallet governs the router or vault.
The wrapper route is demonstrated, not just inferred from getters
Transaction 181c…0fca on 4 September 2026 deposits 30,000 pDAI and issues 29,925 sUSD to
e121. Its successful receipt and 32-call trace agree with the exact existing wrapper and synth identities.
The other four verified deposits are approximately 12,440.445, 41,656.709, 3,973.582 and 48,483.980
pDAI. Full precision stays in the evidence files.
Owned pDAI
   → existing local DAI wrapper
   → existing local sUSD, after mint fee
   → funded Curve / other market
   → pDAI, pUSDC, pUSDT or another accepted market asset
The first two arrows are proved by the historical mints. Curve trading and other sUSD use are also
observed in separate transactions, but this study does not claim to have reconciled every transaction
into one profitable uninterrupted loop. Actual profit, current remaining capacity and outside-dollar
convertibility require their own measurements.
Deposited pDAI becomes redeemable synth collateral. If the operator sells the synth, it cannot continue
counting that collateral as free, exclusively controlled peg inventory. The prior custody audit (Appendix
67) supplies the recorded 20-million-pDAI cap and 14.648-million spare-capacity checkpoint. A
successful 30,000-pDAI mint establishes operation at that historical size; it does not establish 50-billion-
token capacity.
UMA, Across and the simpler integrated thesis
There are several different links:
Across ↔ Optimism asset settlement: the examined October 2024 receipt releases existing local
DAI to Across HubPool using an inherited Optimism proof. This is an actual canonical settlement
connection.
Across ↔ UMA governance: the June 2026 proposal and execution share an assertion ID and
transfer HubPool ownership through its Safe module. The recorded rules exclude HubPool calls; on-
chain settlement is not evidence of a valid Snapshot vote. This authority is distinct from Synthetix
administration.
Synthetix UI ↔ Socket ↔ possible Across routing: Synthetix's bridge announcement and 
Socket's bridge enumeration support an aggregator relationship. They do not prove a presently
funded copied route or an Across permission to issue synths. Synthetix's Q4 2022 report also records
Across governance-related contact.

pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 445

Synthetix ecosystem ↔ UMA discussion: the Q2 2022 report records a joint Thales/UMA event.
That supports historical ecosystem contact; it does not establish that UMA authenticates Synthetix's
native synth bridge.
The UMA perpetual market listed in September 2023 and Chainlink CCIP teleporters launched
in July 2023 are later developments. They are not inherited May 2023 capabilities. A tradable UMA
market is also not an UMA-governed Synthetix issuer. Modern public-network upgrades must be
demonstrated on the copied/private deployment before entering the operative thesis.
The relay and governance study (Appendix 46) retains all eight examined transactions, the confirmed
ownership execution, and proof dates. Synthetix's own owner relay provides a legitimate separate way
for an authorized L1 Safe to administer appropriately owned L2 contracts. The selected public records
still do not prove that the proposed wallet group controls that Safe or the global Optimism messenger.
For peg support, sUSD can be one distribution hub: exact local sUSD → existing Curve bases → the
local stablecoin markets, with Aave and mStable as additional eligible conversions. Purchased pDAI can
return to the demonstrated local wrapper. That reduces the number of issuer changes needed for a first
route. OUSD/eUSD/MIM market access through shared bases is separate from permission to mint those
issuers' coins. Source-side financing on the inaccessible pARB deployment remains an additional,
unverified branch.
Reproduction
Evidence is under artifacts/pulsechain-synthetix-integrations-20261001/. Explicit manifests are Research/
experiments/pulsechain_synthetix_integration_events_20261001.json, 
pulsechain_synthetix_integrations_getters_20261001.json, 
pulsechain_synthetix_registered_integrations_20261001.json, pulsechain_synthetix_integration_runtime_20261001.json
and pulsechain_synthetix_wallet_activity_20261001.json.
python Research/scripts/analyze_pulsechain_synthetix_integrations.py artifacts/pulsechain-synthetix-
integrations-20261001 --output /tmp/synthetix-integration-analysis.json
Use a fresh output path. The command is offline and verifies selected query coverage, receipt-verified
event status, all eleven returned integration settings, wallet event counts, and the five saved mint
traces/deposits/outputs. Getter reproduction must specify --calls; event reproduction uses the explicit
manifest. No state-changing simulation, account impersonation, signature or broadcast is part of the
method.
